name: Six Senses Bhutan
positioning: A collection of five Six Senses lodges across Bhutan's valleys, from hilltop Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Paro to Bumthang further east
best_for: Travelers who want a planned journey across several Bhutanese valleys
Guests interested in Buddhist culture, temples and Himalayan hiking

facts.text: Bhutan lies high in the Eastern Himalayas between India and China.
Six Senses Thimphu is in Babesa, Thimphu.
The Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Paro lodges sit high on hilltops in the Kingdom's western and central valleys.
Six Senses Bumthang is located near the Chamkar Chhu river, further east.
Accommodation is in villas and suites, including three-bedroom villas.
Journeys come with a private guide, driver and vehicle.
Experiences include a sunrise hike to Tiger's Nest and visits to Wangdecholing Palace Museum.
Guests can dine in the Chubjakha Ruin.
Bhutan is described as the world's first carbon-negative country.
Bhutan has chosen low-volume, high-value tourism.

highlights.text: Four of the lodges, Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Paro, sit high on hilltops in Bhutan's western and central valleys.
Guests can stay at one lodge or all five, and Six Senses plans a bespoke journey through the Kingdom.
Guests can light a butter lamp during evening prayers at the 14th-century Damchen Lhakang.
Yoga or meditation is offered at the lodge's Prayer Pavilion.

considerations.text: The five lodges are spread across different valleys, with Bumthang further east, so a full journey involves travel between them.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location requires significant travel time.
